span.label: mechanisms
span.term: adversarial training: a generator and discriminator compete in a minimax game - the generator learns to produce samples that fool the discriminator (which learns real vs fake), driving the generator toward the data distribution
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the likelihood-estimation method has high variance and does not perform well in high dimensions
span.note: what this limits: the reported likelihood numbers: the estimation method DOES NOT PERFORM WELL IN HIGH DIMENSIONAL SPACES
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The model gives no explicit representation of the generator's density, and the discriminator must be kept synchronised with the generator or the generator collapses (the 'Helvetica scenario').
span.note: what this limits: any use requiring a density or stable training: THERE IS NO EXPLICIT REPRESENTATION OF pg(x), AND D MUST BE SYNCHRONIZED WELL WITH G DURING TRAINING
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The Parzen-window likelihood estimate used to evaluate the model is high-variance and performs poorly in high dimensions.
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 0, with the reason it was used anyway: IT HAS SOMEWHAT HIGH VARIANCE AND DOES NOT PERFORM WELL IN HIGH DIMENSIONAL SPACES BUT IT IS THE BEST METHOD AVAILABLE TO OUR KNOWLEDGE
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The convergence result is proved in the non-parametric limit; using a multilayer perceptron for G breaks the theoretical guarantee.
span.note: what this limits: the convergence guarantee, which is proved in the non-parametric limit and does not cover the implementation: USING A MULTILAYER PERCEPTRON TO DEFINE G INTRODUCES MULTIPLE CRITICAL POINTS IN PARAMETER SPACE
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The authors do not claim the generated samples are better than those of existing methods.
span.note: what this limits: any comparison with existing generative models: WHILE WE MAKE NO CLAIM THAT THESE SAMPLES ARE BETTER THAN SAMPLES GENERATED BY EXISTING METHODS, WE BELIEVE THAT THESE SAMPLES ARE AT LEAST COMPETITIVE
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The authors state their evaluation method is high-variance and poor in high dimensions, call it the best available, and report the paper's headline numbers on it.
span.note: what this limits: the log-likelihood figures in Table 1: they come from Gaussian Parzen-window estimation, which the authors say has somewhat high variance and does not perform well in high dimensional spaces
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The convergence results are proved in the non-parametric limit, and the paper states the implementation does not satisfy that condition and has no theoretical guarantee.
span.note: what this limits: the guarantee that pg converges to pdata: it is proved in a non-parametric setting, while the implementation optimises the parameters of a multilayer perceptron, which the paper says lacks theoretical guarantees
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The objective that is trained is not the objective that is analysed; the substitution is made because the analysed one saturates, and the equivalence claimed is of fixed points only.
span.note: what this limits: the relation between Eq. 1 and what was run: G is trained to maximize log D(G(z)) instead, which the paper says gives the same fixed point but much stronger gradients early in learning
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The two stated disadvantages are structural, not incidental: the model has no explicit density, and training can collapse to too few outputs if the two networks fall out of step.
span.note: what this limits: adversarial nets as a density model or as a stable training procedure: there is no explicit representation of pg(x), and D must be synchronized well with G to avoid G collapsing too many values of z to the same value of x
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The claim made for the sample quality is a stated belief, and the paper explicitly declines to claim the samples are better than existing methods.
span.note: what this limits: the figures of generated samples as evidence of quality: the authors make no claim that they are better than existing methods and state only a belief that they are at least competitive
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: a minimax two-player game between a generator and a discriminator, adapting game-theoretic adversarial competition to train generative models
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the displayed samples declared to be FAIR RANDOM DRAWS rather than selected
span.note: eliminates: selection of the best outputs as the basis for judging the model - a figure of hand-picked samples shows what the model CAN do at its best, which is not what the distribution looks like, and nothing in the image itself would reveal the difference
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: a column showing the NEAREST TRAINING EXAMPLE beside each generated sample
span.note: eliminates: memorisation of the training set as the explanation of sample quality - a model that reproduced its training data would look excellent by every visual measure, and the neighbour column is what makes that checkable by the reader
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.
